newsitem.title: USA: Ex-Daiwa trader gets 4 year prison term.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Daiwa trader gets 4 year prison term.

text.p: A former Daiwa Bank Ltd. bond trader was sentenced to four years in prison, fined $2 million and ordered to pay $570,000 in restitution on Monday for hiding losses of $1.1 billion in unauthorized trades and conspiring with managers to conceal one of the greatest financial losses ever.

Toshihide Iguchi, 45, a Japanese-born bond trader who worked in Daiwa Bank's New York office, pleaded guilty in October 1995 at which time he told a federal judge that senior managers at the Japanese bank lied to the Federal Reserve about his activities.

As part of the agreement with prosecutors, Iguchi, who had been senior executive vice president of the bank's New York branch, admitted six counts of misapplication of bank funds, false entries in bank books and records, money laundering and conspiracy. He admitted incurring the trading losses over an 11-year period.
"There is no question that this was a crime of historical dimensions and potentially world shattering implications," said U.S. District Judge Lewis Kaplan in sentencing Iguchi.
